assertions: The PostgreSQL schedule record retained its pinned Prefect execution route.
One independent scheduler process accepted a firing and then lost the durable firing link; a second process remained standby while the first leader lease was held.
After the leader lease was released, a separate scheduler process recovered and linked the existing accepted submission instead of creating a second one.
The recovered accepted submission remained on the schedule's original Prefect execution route, and its route-filtered durable outbox entry remained pending for dispatch.

An amendment that requested route B was rejected while the prior firing remained active; after the canonical attempt completed, the guarded amendment created a new schedule revision on route B and recorded route A as its predecessor.

The PostgreSQL schedule store was reopened in a fresh process-backed adapter; the route-B revision survived, the old firing and completed submission remained on revision/route A, and a subsequent due firing was admitted on route B.
limitations: This proves durable leader/standby and accepted-firing recovery with a pinned Prefect route; it does not start a Prefect flow or qualify a live recurring managed execution.
This adds a managed route-transfer and restart trace to leader/firing recovery; native Prefect trigger rejection and broader schedule outage behavior remain open.
cleanup: The test uses a unique durable store identifier and removes its durable and schedule rows before closing the engine.
